newsitem.title: SURINAM: Surinamese politicians meet to pick new president.
newsitem.headline: Surinamese politicians meet to pick new president.

text.p: Surinamese congressmen and councilors met on Thursday to decide who should run this South American country -- a former school teacher or a leading member of the former military government.

The presidential run-off between incumbent Ronald Venetiaan and Jules Wijdenbosch, right-hand man to former military strongman Desi Bouterse in the 1980s, was expected to be the closest since the South American country gained its independence from the Netherlands in 1975.

A simple majority of the 869-member United Peoples Assembly (VVV), which includes national, regional and district representatives, would be enough to declare either Venetiaan or Wijdenbosch the winner. The assembly is meeting at the national sports centre and results are not expected until about 4 p.m. EDT (2200 GMT).

Venetiaan, 60, had appeared to be the frontrunner after his New Front coalition beat Bouterse's National Democratic Party in national elections in May. But Venetiaan's margin of victory was not wide enough to take control after two voting rounds in the National Assembly and recent defections by New Front members have left him neck-and-neck with Wijdenbosch.

Parties that have joined the NDP-led coalition have done so on condition that Bouterse, 50, will hold no public office. He is held responsible by many for ordering the 1982 torture and murder of 15 opposition leaders.

His stern regime provoked an armed uprising by rebel leader Ronny Brunswijk and the six-year conflict, which started in 1986, killed more than 500 people and led about 15,000 to seek exile in neighbouring French Guiana. Many fear that despite Bouterse's assurances, victory for Wijdenbosch would effectively return the former leader to power.

About 75 former members of Brunswijk's Jungle Commando rebel group met in Paramaribo on Wednesday to express concern an NDP-led government would not stick to promises laid out in a 1992 peace agreement that ended the civil war.
Ties with the Netherlands, virtually broken off during Bouterse's regime, were re-established after Venetiaan's victory in 1991.
Surinam, a small country of 400,000, is one of the biggest bauxite producers in the world.
